literal: The Masters of Writing memorialized approval of the succession to the fief, to clarify the principle of reviving extinct lines.
idiomatic: The Masters of Writing memorialized approval of the succession to the fief, to clarify the principle of reviving extinct lines.

literal: At the time Emperor Xuanwu entrusted government to Gao Zhao; the imperial clan trembled before him—only Kuang stood against Zhao.
idiomatic: At the time Emperor Xuanwu entrusted government to Gao Zhao; the imperial clan trembled before him—only Kuang stood against Zhao.

literal: He had earlier had a coffin made and placed in the reception hall, intending to carry it to the palace gate, denounce Zhao's crimes, and kill himself in desperate remonstrance.
idiomatic: He had earlier had a coffin made and placed in the reception hall, intending to carry it to the palace gate, denounce Zhao's crimes, and kill himself in desperate remonstrance.

literal: Zhao heard of it and hated him.
idiomatic: Zhao heard of it and hated him.

literal: Later, because he disputed weights and measures with Minister of Ceremonies Liu Fang, he clashed with Zhao in voice and manner.
idiomatic: Later, because he disputed weights and measures with Minister of Ceremonies Liu Fang, he clashed with Zhao in voice and manner.

literal: Inspector of the Masters of Writing Wang Xian memorialized against Kuang, saying:
idiomatic: Inspector of the Masters of Writing Wang Xian memorialized against Kuang, saying:

literal: Since the Metal dynasty lost the throne, many usurpers rose together; ritual collapsed and music fell into ruin; the great norms were overturned.
idiomatic: Since the Metal dynasty lost the throne, many usurpers rose together; ritual collapsed and music fell into ruin; the great norms were overturned.

literal: Emperor Gaozu Xiaowen, with sage wisdom ruling heaven, restored the old canons.
idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu Xiaowen, with sage wisdom ruling heaven, restored the old canons.

literal: He then ordered the late Director of the Palace Writers Gao Lu to honor the Confucian schools broadly, search out the Music Office, cut the inch by millet grain, and align with Zhou and Han old statutes.
idiomatic: He then ordered the late Director of the Palace Writers Gao Lu to honor the Confucian schools broadly, search out the Music Office, cut the inch by millet grain, and align with Zhou and Han old statutes.

literal: It happened that the cloud-loom capital moved midway, and the work was not yet complete.
idiomatic: It happened that the cloud-loom capital moved midway, and the work was not yet complete.

literal: Gaozu's wise thought ran deep and dark; consulting classics and records, he took one millet as the measure for fractional parts, made it the standard inch, and promulgated it for use.
idiomatic: Gaozu's wise thought ran deep and dark; consulting classics and records, he took one millet as the measure for fractional parts, made it the standard inch, and promulgated it for use.

literal: By the Zhengshi era the late Director of Music Gongsun Chong on his own authority set twelve grains to the inch, made a separate scale, fixed the laws, and cast the bells.
idiomatic: By the Zhengshi era the late Director of Music Gongsun Chong on his own authority set twelve grains to the inch, made a separate scale, fixed the laws, and cast the bells.

literal: All were nearly finished; he memorialized requesting a trial viewing.
idiomatic: All were nearly finished; he memorialized requesting a trial viewing.

literal: At the time an edict ordered Minister of Ceremonies your subject Fang: since Chong's work was done, gather the court's worthies and debate whether it was acceptable.
idiomatic: At the time an edict ordered Minister of Ceremonies your subject Fang: since Chong's work was done, gather the court's worthies and debate whether it was acceptable.

literal: Fang doubted Chong's scale differed from the prior dynasty; examining its makers, it again diverged from classics and histories—forced invention with thin support, not fit to implement.
idiomatic: Fang doubted Chong's scale differed from the prior dynasty; examining its makers, it again diverged from classics and histories—forced invention with thin support, not fit to implement.

literal: At the time Director of the Masters of Writing your subject Zhao, Prince of Qinghe Yi, and others, holding Chong's work perverse and unlike the Rites of Zhou, memorialized your subject Fang to remake it per the Zhou Rites; when finished, measure and compare, and follow whichever was better.
idiomatic: At the time Director of the Masters of Writing your subject Zhao, Prince of Qinghe Yi, and others, holding Chong's work perverse and unlike the Rites of Zhou, memorialized your subject Fang to remake it per the Zhou Rites; when finished, measure and compare, and follow whichever was better.

literal: But Fang held the prior dynasty's scale consonant with classical antiquity; he followed the earlier edict, cut the inch by millet, and presented it to court for use in bells and stones.
idiomatic: But Fang held the prior dynasty's scale consonant with classical antiquity; he followed the earlier edict, cut the inch by millet, and presented it to court for use in bells and stones.

literal: At the time most debaters said Fang was right.
idiomatic: At the time most debaters said Fang was right.

literal: Only Yellow Gate Attendant your subject Sun Huiwei sided with Chong.
idiomatic: Only Yellow Gate Attendant your subject Sun Huiwei sided with Chong.

literal: The two paths diverged; they were examined again and again.
idiomatic: The two paths diverged; they were examined again and again.

literal: Director of the Masters of Writing your subject Zhao favored Fang's manufacture.
idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing your subject Zhao favored Fang's manufacture.

literal: After Chong died, Huiwei also made a foot-rule, still claiming to support Chong.
idiomatic: After Chong died, Huiwei also made a foot-rule, still claiming to support Chong.

literal: Compared with Chong's foot-rule, they contradicted each other.
idiomatic: Compared with Chong's foot-rule, they contradicted each other.

literal: Measuring and checking two or three times, they deemed Fang's foot-rule correct.
idiomatic: Measuring and checking two or three times, they deemed Fang's foot-rule correct.

literal: But Director of the Masters of Writing your subject Kuang memorialized that the Liu and Sun foot-rules, long and short leaning against each other, when examined against the two pitch-pipes held different capacities; he said to take the middle millet, compare those two houses, and found both irregular—with no mean to strike, he set up his own path and asked for judgment.
idiomatic: But Director of the Masters of Writing your subject Kuang memorialized that the Liu and Sun foot-rules, long and short leaning against each other, when examined against the two pitch-pipes held different capacities; he said to take the middle millet, compare those two houses, and found both irregular—with no mean to strike, he set up his own path and asked for judgment.

literal: Debaters at the time were split for or against Kuang; the two paths clashed and were not settled at once.
idiomatic: Debaters at the time were split for or against Kuang; the two paths clashed and were not settled at once.

literal: Zhao also said, "Weights, bushels, pecks, and foot-rules have long been promulgated; what is debated now cannot exceed the prior intent—we should rely on the prior dynasty's old foot-rule as fixed."
idiomatic: Zhao also said, "Weights, bushels, pecks, and foot-rules have long been promulgated; what is debated now cannot exceed the prior intent—we should rely on the prior dynasty's old foot-rule as fixed."

literal: From then on Kuang and Zhao spoke harshly in the imperial audience hall, voices and faces raised against each other; high and low lost their proper order; honor and rivalry knew no ritual sequence.
idiomatic: From then on Kuang and Zhao spoke harshly in the imperial audience hall, voices and faces raised against each other; high and low lost their proper order; honor and rivalry knew no ritual sequence.

literal: Kuang again memorialized in columns, holding his own ten parts right and Fang's ten parts wrong.
idiomatic: Kuang again memorialized in columns, holding his own ten parts right and Fang's ten parts wrong.

literal: He also said, "Zhao was earlier charged by edict to supervise jointly with Fang, plotting names for bells and stones, hoping to spread the fame of manufacture.
idiomatic: He also said, "Zhao was earlier charged by edict to supervise jointly with Fang, plotting names for bells and stones, hoping to spread the fame of manufacture.

literal: Relying on the weight of the pivot, borrowing his uncle's power, he judged gain and loss by whim, praise and blame by himself, cliqueing with Liu Fang and blocking your subject's business.
idiomatic: Relying on the weight of the pivot, borrowing his uncle's power, he judged gain and loss by whim, praise and blame by himself, cliqueing with Liu Fang and blocking your subject's business.

literal: Those who echoed power he greeted with gracious words;
idiomatic: Those who echoed power he greeted with gracious words;

literal: those who checked classics against antiquity were at once rebuked in anger.
idiomatic: those who checked classics against antiquity were at once rebuked in anger.

literal: Though he has not yet turned deer into horses or moved heaven and shifted the sun, he truly makes refined gentlemen stiffen with fear at their seats;
idiomatic: Though he has not yet turned deer into horses or moved heaven and shifted the sun, he truly makes refined gentlemen stiffen with fear at their seats;

literal: men who cherish the Way bite their tongues at the feast.
idiomatic: men who cherish the Way bite their tongues at the feast.

literal: He also said, "Fang once competed with Chong and always said he made it himself; now debating with your subject he suddenly cites the prior dynasty.
idiomatic: He also said, "Fang once competed with Chong and always said he made it himself; now debating with your subject he suddenly cites the prior dynasty.

literal: Did he not first say it would work and at once seek to take credit himself;
idiomatic: Did he not first say it would work and at once seek to take credit himself;

literal: then, knowing it wrong, push it onto the prior dynasty?
idiomatic: then, knowing it wrong, push it onto the prior dynasty?

literal: This is far from a great minister's bearing and deeply fails the duty of a subordinate.
idiomatic: This is far from a great minister's bearing and deeply fails the duty of a subordinate.

literal: To re-examine before powerful ministers and measure in the hands of the partial—your subject would surely lose his feet in the inner court and hold his jade outside the gate."
idiomatic: To re-examine before powerful ministers and measure in the hands of the partial—your subject would surely lose his feet in the inner court and hold his jade outside the gate."

literal: His clamor ran wild, plain to court and countryside.
idiomatic: His clamor ran wild, plain to court and countryside.

literal: Yet Kuang's duty was intake and output; remonstrance and replacement were his place; pecks, foot-rules, weights, and measures were precisely his office.
idiomatic: Yet Kuang's duty was intake and output; remonstrance and replacement were his place; pecks, foot-rules, weights, and measures were precisely his office.

literal: If he had a view of his own and could judge right and wrong, he ought to have led with the righteous point and early cleared all doubts—why keep silent in heart and follow, not speaking one word, and only after Fang's work was done utter this?
idiomatic: If he had a view of his own and could judge right and wrong, he ought to have led with the righteous point and early cleared all doubts—why keep silent in heart and follow, not speaking one word, and only after Fang's work was done utter this?

literal: Considering Fang's talent and learning, he and Kuang are worlds apart in depth of insight—they should not be matched.
idiomatic: Considering Fang's talent and learning, he and Kuang are worlds apart in depth of insight—they should not be matched.

literal: That he speaks only now—fear this comes from the heart, borrowing others' wisdom to build empty fame.
idiomatic: That he speaks only now—fear this comes from the heart, borrowing others' wisdom to build empty fame.

literal: Moreover Kuang's memorial said, "The bronze weight I rely on matches ancient records in form; clearly it is Han work, not a separate creation of Mang.
idiomatic: Moreover Kuang's memorial said, "The bronze weight I rely on matches ancient records in form; clearly it is Han work, not a separate creation of Mang.

literal: " Examining the weight's inscription: "Yellow Emperor the founding ancestor—his virtue spread in Yu;
idiomatic: " Examining the weight's inscription: "Yellow Emperor the founding ancestor—his virtue spread in Yu;

literal: Yu Emperor the founding ancestor—his virtue spread in Xin."
idiomatic: Yu Emperor the founding ancestor—his virtue spread in Xin."

literal: If this were Mang aiding Han times, how could the inscription bear the false title Xin?
idiomatic: If this were Mang aiding Han times, how could the inscription bear the false title Xin?

literal: Searching Mang's biography, it says when Mang held the regency he at once changed Han institutions.
idiomatic: Searching Mang's biography, it says when Mang held the regency he at once changed Han institutions.

literal: Checking the two proofs, clearly it is not a Han weight.
idiomatic: Checking the two proofs, clearly it is not a Han weight.

literal: He also said, "What Fang made is again shorter than the prior dynasty's foot-rule.
idiomatic: He also said, "What Fang made is again shorter than the prior dynasty's foot-rule.

literal: Your subject has compared them; the weight agrees exactly.
idiomatic: Your subject has compared them; the weight agrees exactly.

literal: He further said, "Fang's foot-rule differs from the Qianjin weir."
idiomatic: He further said, "Fang's foot-rule differs from the Qianjin weir."

literal: Your subject again measured and compared and saw the difference—two or three parts floating loose, hard to use as standard.
idiomatic: Your subject again measured and compared and saw the difference—two or three parts floating loose, hard to use as standard.

literal: He also said, "They jointly built empty ends, falsely made suspicion, claiming the prior dynasty and saying it was not their own manufacture."
idiomatic: He also said, "They jointly built empty ends, falsely made suspicion, claiming the prior dynasty and saying it was not their own manufacture."

literal: Your subject finds this fraud lies in Kuang, not in Fang.
idiomatic: Your subject finds this fraud lies in Kuang, not in Fang.

literal: How so?
idiomatic: How so?

literal: Fang was first charged by edict to specialize in bells and pitch-pipes; the excellence of tubes and reeds was his to judge—weights, bushels, and foot-rules were never his affair.
idiomatic: Fang was first charged by edict to specialize in bells and pitch-pipes; the excellence of tubes and reeds was his to judge—weights, bushels, and foot-rules were never his affair.

literal: Earlier the Palace Secretariat sought Fang's scale; Fang's reply said, "Following the new foot-rule promulgated by the prior dynasty, again applying the lower millet without further increase or decrease—only adjusting fractional parts to make bells and pitch-pipes."
idiomatic: Earlier the Palace Secretariat sought Fang's scale; Fang's reply said, "Following the new foot-rule promulgated by the prior dynasty, again applying the lower millet without further increase or decrease—only adjusting fractional parts to make bells and pitch-pipes."

literal: Checking when Kuang made his rule, it was one year after that reply; on that day Fang and Kuang had not yet disputed—this reply already existed. How call it fraud?
idiomatic: Checking when Kuang made his rule, it was one year after that reply; on that day Fang and Kuang had not yet disputed—this reply already existed. How call it fraud?

literal: Chong's inch used twelve stacked grains—everyone knows it.
idiomatic: Chong's inch used twelve stacked grains—everyone knows it.

literal: Fang's inch used only ten grains—also plain to all.
idiomatic: Fang's inch used only ten grains—also plain to all.

literal: The prior dynasty's edict, making the inch from millet, is clear from start to finish—how could there be a reason to seize it for oneself?
idiomatic: The prior dynasty's edict, making the inch from millet, is clear from start to finish—how could there be a reason to seize it for oneself?

literal: Zhao holds the foremost right seat; the hundred offices look to him—word, act, movement, and stillness must match what all watch.
idiomatic: Zhao holds the foremost right seat; the hundred offices look to him—word, act, movement, and stillness must match what all watch.

literal: If he relies on power, cliques, and fraudulently claims the prior edict, turning deer into horses and shifting sun and day—he is Zhao Gao of Wei; how can he govern things?
idiomatic: If he relies on power, cliques, and fraudulently claims the prior edict, turning deer into horses and shifting sun and day—he is Zhao Gao of Wei; how can he govern things?

literal: If Zhao has none of this, Kuang has slandered the chancellor, mocked current policy, blocked the court's hearing—impiety in the extreme.
idiomatic: If Zhao has none of this, Kuang has slandered the chancellor, mocked current policy, blocked the court's hearing—impiety in the extreme.

literal: We ask that Zhao and Kuang both be barred from the Masters of Writing, the root traced to the end, and the case sent to the Minister of Justice for sentencing.
idiomatic: We ask that Zhao and Kuang both be barred from the Masters of Writing, the root traced to the end, and the case sent to the Minister of Justice for sentencing.

literal: An edict said, "Approved."
idiomatic: An edict said, "Approved."

literal: The relevant offices memorialized that Kuang had slandered Zhao and sentenced Kuang to death.
idiomatic: The relevant offices memorialized that Kuang had slandered Zhao and sentenced Kuang to death.

literal: Emperor Xuanwu spared his life and reduced him to Honored Grandee of Light.
idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu spared his life and reduced him to Honored Grandee of Light.

literal: He was also made Grand Master of the Imperial Clan.
idiomatic: He was also made Grand Master of the Imperial Clan.

literal: He went out as governor of Yanzhou.
idiomatic: He went out as governor of Yanzhou.

literal: As Kuang was about to depart, the emperor received him in the Eastern Hall and comforted him.
idiomatic: As Kuang was about to depart, the emperor received him in the Eastern Hall and comforted him.

literal: Kuang still held that scales, foot-rules, bells, and stones were great statutes of state; though the Southern Terrace had impeached him before, he was still allowed further debate.
idiomatic: Kuang still held that scales, foot-rules, bells, and stones were great statutes of state; though the Southern Terrace had impeached him before, he was still allowed further debate.

literal: If there is a day of debate, I beg leave to attend briefly.
idiomatic: If there is a day of debate, I beg leave to attend briefly.

literal: The emperor said, "Liu Fang's learning tops his age; he is deep in ancient precedent.
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Liu Fang's learning tops his age; he is deep in ancient precedent.

literal: What he relies on differs from the prior dynasty's foot-rule by only one millet per inch—how can he again say it is the prior dynasty's intent?"
idiomatic: What he relies on differs from the prior dynasty's foot-rule by only one millet per inch—how can he again say it is the prior dynasty's intent?"

literal: Yanzhou is already what you hold without warrant; on the day of later debate, why wait to come to the capital?"
idiomatic: Yanzhou is already what you hold without warrant; on the day of later debate, why wait to come to the capital?"

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he entered as Inspector of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he entered as Inspector of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Kuang was severe in impeachment; he first memorialized against Yu Zhong, then against Gao Cong and others for removal—all were denied by Empress Dowager Ling.
idiomatic: Kuang was severe in impeachment; he first memorialized against Yu Zhong, then against Gao Cong and others for removal—all were denied by Empress Dowager Ling.

literal: Thwarted in his wish to impeach the wicked, and fearing Kuang would resign, she wished to reward and reassure him—advanced to General Who Pacifies the South, later added General Who Guards the East.
idiomatic: Thwarted in his wish to impeach the wicked, and fearing Kuang would resign, she wished to reward and reassure him—advanced to General Who Pacifies the South, later added General Who Guards the East.

literal: Whenever Kuang had a memorial request, Director of the Masters of Writing Prince of Rencheng Cheng would often seize and block it.
idiomatic: Whenever Kuang had a memorial request, Director of the Masters of Writing Prince of Rencheng Cheng would often seize and block it.

literal: Kuang was harsh and narrow; inwardly he grew resentful.
idiomatic: Kuang was harsh and narrow; inwardly he grew resentful.

literal: The coffin he had made earlier was still at a monastery; he again prepared matters, intending to clash with Cheng.
idiomatic: The coffin he had made earlier was still at a monastery; he again prepared matters, intending to clash with Cheng.

literal: Cheng learned of it somewhat; later, going to the Secretariat, he met Kuang by chance—their outriders beat each other; court and countryside were appalled.
idiomatic: Cheng learned of it somewhat; later, going to the Secretariat, he met Kuang by chance—their outriders beat each other; court and countryside were appalled.

literal: Cheng therefore memorialized more than thirty counts against Kuang; the Minister of Justice sentenced him to death.
idiomatic: Cheng therefore memorialized more than thirty counts against Kuang; the Minister of Justice sentenced him to death.

literal: An edict referred it to the eightfold deliberation; he was specially pardoned, stripped of rank and office.
idiomatic: An edict referred it to the eightfold deliberation; he was specially pardoned, stripped of rank and office.

literal: Senior Gentleman of the Three Excellencies Xin Xiong memorialized to judge the case.
idiomatic: Senior Gentleman of the Three Excellencies Xin Xiong memorialized to judge the case.

literal: Later he was specially appointed governor of Pingzhou, then transferred to Qingzhou.
idiomatic: Later he was specially appointed governor of Pingzhou, then transferred to Qingzhou.

literal: Soon he was made Commander of the Guanxi region and acting Director of the Masters of Writing on the Mobile Office.
idiomatic: Soon he was made Commander of the Guanxi region and acting Director of the Masters of Writing on the Mobile Office.

literal: He fell ill and returned to the capital.
idiomatic: He fell ill and returned to the capital.

literal: In the beginning of Xiaochang he died; posthumous name Wen Zhen.
idiomatic: In the beginning of Xiaochang he died; posthumous name Wen Zhen.

literal: Later his original rank was posthumously restored and he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Jinan.
idiomatic: Later his original rank was posthumously restored and he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Jinan.
